ground_truth_witness: Let L={0,a,b,c,1}, ordered by 0<a,b,c<1 with a,b,c pairwise incomparable (the five-element diamond M₃). It is a complete lattice: finite joins and meets exist; distinct atoms join to 1 and meet to 0. But a ∧ (b ∨ c)=a ∧ 1=a, whereas (a ∧ b) ∨ (a ∧ c)=0 ∨ 0=0. Since a≠0, finite meet does not distribute over arbitrary join, so L is not a frame.
ground_truth_flaw: Every complete lattice is an object of Frm, so CLat is a subcategory of Frm.
